2.name: text_block

0.name: block
0.value:
Smooths streams of quaternions with a Kalman filter that caps how far any one frame can turn it.

Use it on mocap joint rotations that are mostly clean but now and then throw a frame that is wildly wrong. The glitch moves the output by no more than 'max jump' degrees, so it barely shows.

HOW IT WORKS:
It works in the rotation's own terms (an error-state filter, like t.quat_ESEKF): it keeps an orientation and an angular velocity per joint, predicts the next frame, and measures the difference from the input as a small rotation - the INNOVATION. Two caps are applied before the correction is used:

  max jump      the innovation is shortened to at most this many degrees
  max_accel     the whole correction is scaled down if the angular
                acceleration it implies is above this. The limit is
                relaxed up to 50 times while the joint is already turning
                fast (from about 60 to 85 degrees a second), so it is
                strict at rest, where a sudden jump is most likely a
                glitch, and lenient in motion.

A real quick turn bigger than max jump is followed a bounded bite at a time, so it takes several frames. Unlike t.quat_ESEKF there are no modes: the same settings always apply.

MANY STREAMS AT ONCE:
The input is a tensor of shape [streams, values]: one row per stream, all of them one moment in time. Every row gets its own filter state, so a whole body - 22 joints, one row each - is filtered in one operation. The first frame (and any change in the number of rows) builds the state afresh.
The quaternions are w x y z, w first (as euler_to_quaternion makes them), one row per joint: shape [joints, 4].

SYNTAX:
t.smart_clamp_quat_kf
No arguments.

EXAMPLE:
t.smart_clamp_quat_kf

INPUTS and PARAMETERS:

input:
[joints, 4], w first; a single quaternion [4] is accepted and comes back as [4]. Anything else is ignored. Each arrival runs one step and sends.

responsiveness (float, default 1.0):
The process noise: how freely the turning speed may change. Higher follows changes sooner and smooths less.

smoothness (float, default 0.1):
The measurement noise: how much each reading is distrusted. Higher smooths more and lags more.

max jump (deg) (float, default 5):
The largest correction used in one frame, in degrees. 0 turns this cap off.

accel_rejection (float, default 0, off):
When the estimated angular acceleration reverses from one frame to the next, divide the process noise by (1 + 100 x this).

max_accel (deg/s^2) (float, default 50000):
The second cap: the angular acceleration a correction may imply. With the default the size cap does almost all the work; lower this (to a few thousand) to make the acceleration cap matter.

reset (button):
The next input becomes the orientation outright, at rest. The filter also starts this way, from its first input.

dt (float, default 1/60):
The time between frames. Zero or less is taken as 1/60.

OUTPUTS:

filtered:
The filtered quaternions, [joints, 4], unit length.

READING THE DEMO:
Measured on this input at the default 5 degrees: a 45 degree glitch moves the output by only a degree or two; the jitter is about a sixth of the input's; each 30 degree quick turn takes around ten frames to be followed. Drag max jump on the node: at 20 the turns are followed in three or four frames but an eighth of each glitch shows; at 2 a turn takes twenty frames and the output trails even the slow turning.

THE GLITCH OR THE MOVEMENT:
A tracker throws two kinds of sudden change: a GLITCH, one bad frame that comes straight back, and a real QUICK MOVEMENT, a change that stays. On the frame it happens they look the same. Any filter that refuses the glitch will also hesitate on the quick movement; the filters in this family differ in how they make that bet. The demo input has both, so you can see each filter's choice.

THE FAMILY:
t.ESEKF            ordinary numbers, three modes blended by motion
t.quat_ESEKF       the same for quaternions (error-state)
t.smart_clamp_kf   ordinary numbers, the correction per frame capped
t.smart_clamp_quat_kf      the same for quaternions, plus an acceleration cap
t.persistence_quat_kf      acceleration cap that gives way if the change persists
t.hybrid_quat_kf   three-mode blending driving a smart-clamped filter

RELATED:
t.persistence_quat_kf is this filter with a different acceleration cap:
it lets a change through once it has lasted a few frames. t.smart_clamp_kf is the version for ordinary numbers.
